title: What the Section and the Scatter Saw — Tissue Biopsy, Cold Ischemia & Margin Geometry (H029), Flow Cytometry Clonality, MRD & Lineage Switch (H030) & Veterinary Helical CT Staging (V016)

teenKit.tldr: Medical scans and tissue samples aren't transparent windows into the body; they are funhouse mirrors warped by physics, chemistry, and human handling. This episode explores how tiny diagnostic illusions and machine artifacts shape the human and veterinary diagnoses we rely on.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding that diagnostic tools create artifacts reminds us that science is an active interpretation of nature, not an absolute playback of reality.
keyTakeaways: Every diagnostic step—from the moment tissue loses its blood supply to the chemicals used to preserve it—physically warps the biological truth.
Human surgical histopathology preserves spatial tissue architecture, while flow cytometry completely destroys that architecture to analyze single cells at the speed of light.
Veterinary helical CT bridges the gap by providing volumetric 3D imaging to track macro-level diseases like canine lung nodules and vascular shunts.

vocab.meaning: The critical window of time when a tissue sample has been removed from the body but has not yet been preserved in chemicals, causing cellular stress.
A high-speed laser technique that blasts single cells with light to analyze them individually, requiring the destruction of the original tissue layout.
An advanced scanning technology where the X-ray machine rotates continuously in a spiral to capture high-resolution 3D volumes of the body.
A false structural or visual feature created by the diagnostic tools themselves rather than being part of the actual disease.
